remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor only narrowed and reframed the same BPROC-014-A through BPROC-014-E record.

The policy predicate for rejection is still unmet on the summarized record because no admissible item expressly shows the unresolved issue was assessed as material enough to support rejection rather than follow-up or escalation.
The cited facts remain the kinds of quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies that policy says justify follow-up or escalation by themselves, not reject-level action.
Evidence access is limited to the Actor summary only, so there is still no independent basis to verify timing, materiality, or whether any formally logged security conclusion exists.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor's response is a narrower interpretation of the same evidence, not new admissible evidence. That reinterpretation usefully concedes that the record does not prove a reject-level control failure and that clean compliance is not supportable without a formal materiality link. But the audited claim is still that rejection was policy-compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk at decision time. On the available summary, that support link remains missing. A caveated description such as 'approval was not ready pending further diligence' is closer to the evidence, but it is not the same as proving that outright rejection satisfied the policy standard. Because the unresolved caveat is itself the core compliance predicate, this is not enough for compliant_with_caveats.
